quizzes.title: Module 1 Quiz: Starting Out as an AI-Powered VA

questions.text: What does an AI-Powered VA primarily do?
choices: Uses AI tools to complete business tasks faster while still applying judgment and quality checks
Builds AI models from scratch for clients
Only forwards whatever a chatbot outputs without review
Repairs computer hardware

questions.text: Why do businesses hire an AI-Powered VA instead of just using AI tools themselves?
choices: AI tools are illegal for small businesses to use directly
They want the time savings of AI without learning prompt engineering and tool setup themselves
AI tools cannot be used by businesses at all
It is required by freelance platforms

questions.text: Which trait most separates a professional AI VA from someone who just copy-pastes chatbot replies?
choices: Typing speed
Catching and correcting AI mistakes before they reach a client
Using only one AI tool ever
Avoiding all client communication

questions.text: When a client says 'use AI for this,' what do they usually actually mean?
choices: They want a specific AI tool installed on their computer
They want the result faster or cheaper - not necessarily a specific technology
They want to learn prompt engineering themselves
They are testing whether you know a programming language

questions.text: What is a reasonable minimum setup to start practicing as an AI VA?
choices: An expensive dedicated AI workstation
A reliable computer and free accounts on tools like ChatGPT and Claude
A university degree in computer science
A paid subscription to every AI tool that exists

questions.text: What are ChatGPT and Claude best described as?
choices: General-purpose AI assistants strong at writing, research, and reasoning
Spreadsheet software
Video editing tools only
Password managers

questions.text: What is prompt engineering?
choices: A type of computer programming language
Writing clear, specific instructions that get useful results from an AI tool
Repairing broken AI models
A certification required to use ChatGPT

questions.text: What do Zapier and Make primarily help you do?
choices: Connect different apps so information flows between them automatically
Design company logos
Process client payments
Write legal contracts

questions.text: In Zapier, what is a 'Zap' made of?
choices: Only a trigger, with no further action
A trigger and one or more actions
A chatbot script
A billing invoice

questions.text: What is Grammarly best used for in an AI VA's workflow?
choices: Generating the entire first draft from scratch
A final quality pass on grammar, tone, and clarity
Building automations
Scheduling social media posts

questions.text: What should you always confirm before using AI-generated images in client-facing content?
choices: Nothing - AI images are always safe to use anywhere
That the client is comfortable with AI-generated imagery
The exact pixel dimensions only
Whether the image tool has a mobile app

questions.text: What is the recommended approach to building your AI toolkit?
choices: Master every AI tool that exists immediately
Focus on a handful of tools that fit your niche and add more as real needs arise
Use only one tool forever, regardless of the task
Avoid learning any new tools after your first month

quizzes.title: Module 3 Quiz: Core AI VA Skills

questions.text: Before sending an AI-drafted email reply, what should you always do?
choices: Send it immediately with no review
Give it a quick tone check to make sure it fits the relationship
Delete it and start over every time
Forward it to a random colleague

questions.text: When using AI for research, why must you still verify facts?
choices: AI can state incorrect information confidently, known as hallucination
AI research is always illegal to use
Verification is only needed for numbers, never names or claims
It isn't necessary if the AI sounds confident

questions.text: What is the best first step before building any automation?
choices: Open Zapier immediately and start clicking
Write out the workflow in plain language first, identifying the trigger and each action
Skip planning since automations rarely need structure
Ask the client to build it themselves

questions.text: What should any basic business chatbot always include?
choices: No way to reach a human under any circumstance
A clear, easy path for a visitor to reach a real human when needed
Only Yes/No answers
Access to the client's full financial records

questions.text: What content types deserve extra-careful human review before publishing?
choices: Casual social captions only
Content with specific client facts, sensitive announcements, or legal/medical/financial claims
Nothing - all AI content is safe to publish as-is
Only content written on weekends

questions.text: What is the safest habit regarding client data and public AI tools?
choices: Paste anything into any AI tool without checking
Never paste sensitive client data into a public AI tool without understanding its data policy, and ask the client when in doubt
Only worry about data privacy for large companies
Assume all AI tools delete data instantly with no exceptions

quizzes.title: Module 4 Quiz: Building Your AI VA Portfolio

questions.text: What is a 'mock project' used for in an AI VA portfolio?
choices: A real paid client project
A sample project created to demonstrate your skills before you have paid clients
A type of scam
A required legal document

questions.text: How should mock projects be labeled in a portfolio?
choices: As real client results with no disclaimer
Clearly and honestly as sample or practice work
They should never be shown to anyone
As guaranteed outcomes for future clients

questions.text: What is often the clearest success metric an AI VA can show?
choices: The number of AI tools they own
Time saved on a task, shown honestly as a before/after comparison
How many hours they worked, regardless of output
The size of the AI model used

questions.text: Which free-or-low-cost options work well for hosting a simple AI VA portfolio?
choices: Carrd, Notion, or a well-organized Google Drive folder
Only expensive custom-built websites
None exist for free
Only printed paper portfolios

questions.text: Why should you document your process (prompts, automation steps) in a portfolio, not just the final result?
choices: It has no value to a future client
Clients want to understand how you think and work, not just see a finished output
It is required by AI tool terms of service
It replaces the need for any actual skills

questions.text: What should an AI VA resume bullet point focus on?
choices: Vague statements with no detail
Specific tools and quantified results, like estimated time saved
Only job titles
Personal hobbies unrelated to the role

questions.text: What makes a strong proposal for an AI-related job posting?
choices: A generic copy-paste message mentioning 'AI' in general terms
Personalization that identifies their specific repetitive task or bottleneck
Extremely long, unfocused paragraphs
No mention of relevant tools or skills

questions.text: Which platforms are commonly used to find AI VA clients?
choices: Upwork and Onlinejobs.ph, filtering for AI/automation roles
Only local newspapers
Random unrelated apps
None, clients cannot be found online

questions.text: What is a good goal during a discovery call with a potential AI VA client?
choices: Avoid asking any questions
Understand their current workflow, past frustrations, and who needs to approve the work
Immediately demand payment before speaking
Refuse to discuss their business

questions.text: Why should you never list a tool on your resume that you haven't actually practiced with?
choices: It doesn't matter, clients never check
Clients in this niche often test your tool knowledge on the spot
Tools listed on a resume are legally binding
There is no reason, it is just a suggestion

quizzes.title: Module 6 Quiz: Landing Your First Client and Beyond

questions.text: What is a good first step when onboarding a new AI VA client?
choices: Guess what they want without asking
Get minimum necessary account access safely and gather the context AI tools will need
Immediately increase your rate
Avoid all communication in week one

questions.text: Which is a common pricing model for AI VA services?
choices: Monthly retainer
Random guessing
Refusing to state a price
Charging only in a currency you don't understand

questions.text: What is a basic security habit every AI VA should follow?
choices: Share one login across all clients for convenience
Use a password manager and turn on two-factor authentication wherever offered
Write down passwords on paper and keep them at a client's office
Avoid using any organizational tools

questions.text: How should an AI VA respond to 'this doesn't sound like us' feedback on AI-drafted content?
choices: Argue that the client is wrong
Ask for a specific example that does sound right and update saved style notes
Ignore the feedback completely
Stop using AI tools entirely for that client

questions.text: What helps build a long-term AI VA career?
choices: Refusing to learn new tools or stay current
Going deeper into key tools, staying current with new releases, and asking for testimonials
Never asking for client feedback
Avoiding all specialization
